answer: Yes. The subtext enriches the story’s setting and characterization rather than feeling forced. Q’s description of layoffs as “an editorial process” reveals how polished corporate language disguises cruelty, while the exclusive poolside setting exposes his assumption that comfort and privilege can make an unjust decision “civilized.” Meredith’s blazer and portfolio contrast with his leisurewear, quietly emphasizing their unequal stakes in the meeting. The narrator’s final relief suggests release from years of feeling inferior to Q—not merely satisfaction at witnessing an awkward dismissal.
